source: 我不想再努力了，我要躺平。
intended_meaning: I don't want to keep pushing myself; I'm opting out of the rat race.
raw_translation: I don't want to try anymore. I'm going to lay flat.
refined: I don't want to work hard anymore; I'm just gonna lie down.
reason: "lay flat" is a literal mistranslation of the slang "躺平" (tang ping), which means giving up and relaxing/idling rather than literally lying on the ground.

source: 现在工作太卷了，我想躺平。
intended_meaning: Work is so cutthroat now that I just want to opt out.
raw_translation: Now the job's too curly, I'd like to lay flat.
refined: Nowadays work is so competitive that I just want to lie down and do nothing.
reason: "卷" means being overly competitive or cutthroat; "躺平" is slang for giving up on striving and doing the bare minimum. The translation was a literal mistranslation of these idioms.

source: 我们公司太内卷了，大家都加班到十点。
intended_meaning: My company is hyper-competitive; everyone works overtime until 10.
raw_translation: We're too introverted. We're all working till 10:00.
refined: Our company is so competitive that everyone works until ten.
reason: "内卷" means internal competition/rat race in a work context; "introverted" refers to personality traits

source: 看到那个视频我直接破防了。
intended_meaning: That video hit me hard emotionally.
raw_translation: I just broke it when I saw that video.
refined: I completely lost my mind after seeing that video.
reason: "broke" is slang for losing composure or mental stability; "破防" was translated literally as breaking something

source: 我是社恐，不想去那个聚会。
intended_meaning: I'm socially anxious/awkward, so I don't want to go to that party.
raw_translation: I'm scared. I don't want to go to that party.
refined: I have social anxiety, so I don't want to go to that party.
reason: "社恐" is a specific slang term for having social anxiety; "scared" alone misses the nuance of being uncomfortable in social situations rather than just afraid.

source: 打工人又要上班了。
intended_meaning: Back to the grind again (self-deprecating joke about being a worker).
raw_translation: Beating the workers is going to work again.
refined: Workers are back at work.
reason: "Beating" and "work" were mistranslated from slang terms; corrected meaning of '打工人' as a self-deprecating term for employees and '上班' as going to work.

source: 别凡尔赛了，你明明考得很好。
intended_meaning: Stop humblebragging, you obviously did great on the exam.
raw_translation: Oh, come on, Versailles. You did a great job.
refined: Stop being so modest; you clearly scored very well.
reason: "Van Rosse" is slang for pretending to be humble when one has achieved something good (often by downplaying it). The translation treated 'Versailles' as a proper noun/name rather than the idiom. Also corrected the tone from condescending ('Oh, come on') to supportive/teasing based on context.

source: 他对考试很佛系。
intended_meaning: He's very laid-back about exams and doesn't stress.
raw_translation: He's very Buddhist in his exams.
refined: He is quite laid-off about the exam.
reason: "佛系" means "laid-back" or "carefree", not literally related to Buddhism; 'buddhist' was a mistranslation of this slang

source: 我就是来吃瓜的。
intended_meaning: I'm just here to watch the drama.
raw_translation: I'm here to eat melons.
refined: I'm just here for the gossip.
reason: "eat melon" is a slang idiom meaning to watch or listen in on others' business; translated literally as eating actual fruit

source: 这个价格太离谱了。
intended_meaning: This price is ridiculous.
raw_translation: This price is ridiculous.
refined: This price is outrageous.
reason: "outrageous" better captures the strong negative emotion of "离谱" than just "ridiculous", which can sound milder or slightly different in tone.

source: 这个游戏太上头了。
intended_meaning: This game is so addictive.
raw_translation: This game is too high.
refined: This game is so addictive.
reason: "上头" is slang for being extremely engaging or addictive; "too high" was a literal mistranslation

source: 这家火锅yyds！
intended_meaning: This hotpot place is the best / the GOAT.
raw_translation: This fire potyds!
refined: This hotpot is yyds!
reason: "fire" was a mistranslation of "hot", and the sentence structure should match the source's casual tone

source: 我今天有点emo。
intended_meaning: I'm feeling kind of down today.
raw_translation: I'm a little emo today.
refined: I feel a bit down today.
reason: "emo" is slang for feeling sad or blue; "a little emo" sounds unnatural in English and the literal meaning doesn't capture the emotional state intended.

source: 这个菜绝了！
intended_meaning: This dish is amazing!
raw_translation: This one's perfect!
refined: This dish is amazing!
reason: "绝了" implies something is outstanding or incredible; "perfect" is too mild and misses the enthusiastic tone.

source: 我昨天去找他了，但是不在。
intended_meaning: I went to see him yesterday, but he wasn't there.
raw_translation: I went to see him yesterday, but I wasn't there.
refined: I went to see him yesterday, but he wasn't home.
reason: source implies the person sought was absent; machine translation incorrectly states the speaker was not present

source: 昨天给他发消息，一直没回。
intended_meaning: I texted him yesterday and he never replied.
raw_translation: I sent him a message yesterday, and I haven't returned.
refined: I texted him yesterday, but he hasn't replied.
reason: Source implies the speaker sent the message while 'he' did not reply; translation incorrectly made the subject of 'haven't returned' refer to the sender

source: 我去她家找她，结果不在家。
intended_meaning: I went to her place, but she wasn't home.
raw_translation: I went to her house to find her, and I wasn't home.
refined: I went to her house to look for her, but she wasn't there.
reason: Source implies the speaker visited someone else's house; translation incorrectly made the speaker 'not at home'

source: 这个 project 的 deadline 是明天。
intended_meaning: This project's deadline is tomorrow.
raw_translation: This project's deadline is tomorrow.
refined: This project's deadline is tomorrow.
reason: accurate and natural

source: 我明天有个 meeting，不能去了。
intended_meaning: I have a meeting tomorrow, so I can't go.
raw_translation: I have a meeting tomorrow. I can't go.
refined: I have a meeting tomorrow, so I can't make it.
reason: Added 'so' to connect the cause and effect naturally; changed 'go' to 'make it' which is more idiomatic for attending an event

source: 今天天气很好。
intended_meaning: The weather is nice today.
raw_translation: It's a nice day.
refined: It's a lovely day.
reason: "nice" is slightly weak for "好" in this context; "lovely" better captures the positive tone of good weather.

source: 你吃饭了吗？
intended_meaning: Have you eaten? (often used as a casual greeting)
raw_translation: Have you eaten yet?
refined: Have you eaten?
reason: The source is a common greeting rather than asking about the specific timing 'yet', so removing 'yet' makes it more natural.

source: No cap, that exam was brutal.
intended_meaning: Honestly, that exam was really hard.
raw_translation: 没有帽子,那考试是残酷的。
refined: 没开玩笑，那场考试太难了。
reason: "No cap" is slang for "no joke" or "for real," not literally about a hat; the translation corrected this literal mistranslation and adjusted the register to match casual speech.

source: I'm lowkey tired of this class.
intended_meaning: I'm kind of / secretly tired of this class.
raw_translation: 我受够这班了
refined: 我对这门课有点烦。
reason: "lowkey" indicates a mild or understated feeling; "受够" is too strong as it means 'done with' completely. The translation should reflect the casual but moderate tone of being slightly tired/bored.

source: Your outfit is giving main character.
intended_meaning: Your outfit makes you look confident, like the star of the show.
raw_translation: 你的衣服是给主人物。
refined: 你这身穿搭很有主角感。
reason: "giving" in this context means "exhibits the quality of," and "main character energy/style" is a common internet slang phrase. The literal translation was grammatically incorrect and missed the idiomatic meaning.

source: That movie was mid.
intended_meaning: That movie was mediocre.
raw_translation: 那部电影是中间的。
refined: 那部片子很一般/没意思。
reason: "mid" is slang for mediocre or average; the literal translation "中间" does not convey this meaning.

source: Bet, I'll see you at six.
intended_meaning: Okay, sounds good, I'll see you at six.
raw_translation: 我打赌,六点见
refined: 走着瞧，六点钟见。
reason: "Bet" is used here as a confident prediction or challenge rather than an actual wager; "走著瞧" captures this tone better. Also added the implied subject for natural flow.

source: That guy is acting kind of sus.
intended_meaning: That guy is acting kind of suspicious.
raw_translation: 那家伙表现得有点像苏斯
refined: 这家伙有点可疑。
reason: "sus" is slang for suspicious; the machine translated it literally as "Susie/Sus", which makes no sense in this context.

source: She ghosted me after our first date.
intended_meaning: She stopped replying without explanation after our first date.
raw_translation: 我们第一次约会后,她就把我鬼鬼祟祟了
refined: 我们在第一次约会后就被她甩了。
reason: "ghost" is slang for abruptly cutting off contact without explanation; "摆烂/消失" was mistranslated as "鬼鬼祟祟 (sneaky)" which changes the meaning

source: I'm dead, that video was so funny.
intended_meaning: I'm laughing so hard, that video was so funny.
raw_translation: 我死了,那视频太好笑了。
refined: 我笑死我了，那个视频太好笑了。
reason: "I'm dead" is slang for laughing uncontrollably; the literal translation "I died" changes the meaning

source: Break a leg tonight!
intended_meaning: Good luck with your performance tonight!
raw_translation: 祝今晚好运!
refined: 祝你今晚演出顺利！
reason: "Break a leg" is an idiom wishing someone success in their performance; the literal meaning of "good luck" doesn't capture this specific context.

source: Can you pass me the salt?
intended_meaning: Can you pass me the salt?
raw_translation: 能把盐递给我吗?
refined: 能帮我拿把盐吗？
reason: "pass" in this context means to hand over an object rather than deliver it; "递" is slightly formal for a casual request like this. Using "拿" (pick up/get) fits the natural flow better.
